html:
The White Horde was the eastern half of the Mongol lands of Jochi, Genghis Khan's eldest son. It covered the steppe of today's Kazakhstan, from the Ural River to the Syr Darya and the Irtysh. Jochi's son Orda received it around 1225, while his brother Batu took the western half, which became the Golden Horde. Medieval sources mix up the names White and Blue Horde, so writers use them in different ways.

For over a century the White Horde stood loosely under the Golden Horde. In the 1370s its khan Urus Khan grew strong. His rival Tokhtamysh, backed by Timur, took the White Horde and then united it with the Golden Horde around 1380, and in 1382 he burned Moscow in the siege of Moscow. Timur later turned on him and crushed him in the 1390s.

In the 1400s the eastern steppe passed to Abu'l-Khayr Khan and his Uzbeks. Two descendants of Urus Khan broke away from him with their followers and founded the Kazakh Khanate around 1465.
